### REQ-013: Fix self-deadlock in message-queue processing (get → sendStatus re-lock)

## Requirement

`Room::updateControl()` and `Thermo::updateControl()` hold their non-recursive `std::mutex` while draining the message queue. A `room_get`/`device_get` message with a `status` payload makes `Configurable::processMessage()` call the virtual `sendStatus()`, which locks the **same** mutex again (`core/room.cpp:131` → `configurable.cpp:71` → `room.cpp:240`; analogous in `core/thermo.cpp:76` → `thermo.cpp:117`). Double-locking a non-recursive `std::mutex` deadlocks: the control task freezes while holding `Thermo::mutex_`, which then blocks the sensor and UI tasks — total firmware freeze, remotely triggerable by publishing `{"status":true}` to `cmd/<deviceId>/get` or `cmd/<room>/get`.

Root cause: `processMessageQueue()` runs inside the locked region and re-enters locked public methods. Fix by restructuring so message handling never re-acquires the state lock — e.g. drain the queue outside the lock and take the lock only inside individual field-update handlers, or split status/config sending into "build JSON under lock" + "publish unlocked" and ensure `processMessage()` uses only the unlocked variants.

See finding F-1 in `doc/reports/2026-07-02_migration_code_review.md`.

## Notes

Consider a debug assertion (owner-tracking) around the mutexes to catch future re-entry regressions.
